clue.text: River mouth? It could be Shannon, thanks

parts.note: Del Shannon was the American singer of Runaway, so Shannon could be Del
ta is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: A geography question: could the mouth of a river be Ireland's Shannon, thank you?
explanation.walkthrough: Shannon looks like the Irish river, but it is the surname of the singer Del Shannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan of silt and channels where a river meets the sea, so it is a kind of mouth.

clue.text: Upset, say, Sir Ken's endless scam

indicators.note: endless says the comedian's surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Sir Ken Dodd was a famous Liverpool comedian

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the abbreviation for example is turned upside down

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a scam run by a famous comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a British comedian knighted in 2017; DODD loses its last letter to give DOD, followed by GE (EG upset).
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or swindle, so it is a synonym for a scam.

clue.text: Drunk in awful hole somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: in says the drunkard is placed inside the rearranged letters
awful says the letters of hole are messed up into a new order

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk ends up in a dreadful hole somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective for the hole's state, but it is a noun, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, so it is a place in Africa.

clue.text: Chief section of the foot

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, chief or principal
the curved part of the sole between heel and ball

explanation.surface: An anatomy note about the most important part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch serves both as a prefix-like adjective meaning principal and as the name of the foot's curved underside.

clue.text: Sticky sandwich to stuff still empty tummy

parts.note: to jam is to cram or stuff
but can mean still or yet, as in 'but I went anyway'

indicators.note: empty says only the outside letters of tummy are kept

explanation.surface: A sweet sandwich to fill a tummy that is still empty.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is northern British slang for a sandwich, so a jam butty is bread and jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread spread with jam is a sticky snack, and butty is a British word for a sandwich.

clue.text: Jack — how can I put this? — Rogers sheep in Australia

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
um is the hesitation sound of someone searching for words
Buck Rogers is the science fiction space hero

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly says that a man named Jack Rogers is a sheep in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The aside 'how can I put this?' reads like an interruption, but it gives the hesitation UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbuck is Australian slang for a sheep, familiar from the song Waltzing Matilda.

clue.text: Country cricket club on no runs after second run-out

indicators.note: after says the cricket club and duck come after the second and run-out
on says in this down clue the club sits on top of the zero

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
O is zero, a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: A county cricket club scores nothing after an early run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' could be misread as 'County'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a North African nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Full, hazy sun suffusing colour

indicators.note: suffusing says the jumbled sun spreads over and leads into the colouring word
hazy says the letters of sun are blurred into a new order

parts.note: to colour something is tinting it

explanation.surface: A full picture of a hazy sun flooding the sky with colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazy' rearranges SUN to UNS, which runs straight into TINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstinting praise or support is given lavishly without holding back, so it is full and generous.

clue.text: Oberon's wife isn't commonly up and about at one

indicators.note: about says the colloquial word goes around the next letters
in a down clue, up says the colloquial word is read from the bottom

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
at followed by I, the Roman numeral one, also read from the bottom up, as 'up' governs the whole

explanation.surface: Oberon's wife is awake and about at one o'clock in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: As the blogger noted, 'up' must also turn 'at one' (AT, I) to ITA. 'isn't commonly' is the dialect ain't.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the fairy queen married to Oberon is Titania.

clue.text: Lewd Soho burlesque in which Shearer strips 4D?

indicators.note: burlesque, a parody or striptease show, says the letters are sent up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lewd Soho burlesque show in which footballer Alan Shearer strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: Shearer looks like the footballer Alan Shearer; here it is a sheep-shearer, and 4D is JUMBUCK, an Australian sheep. Soho is London's old red-light district.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolshed is the Australian farm building where sheep are shorn of their fleeces.

clue.text: Vicious setback for underworld figure

indicators.note: setback says the first name is set back, read from right to left

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the bassist of the Sex Pistols

explanation.surface: A cruel reversal for a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld figure' suggests a criminal, but it is the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman ruler of the realm of the dead, equivalent to Pluto or Hades.

clue.text: Combined with copper money

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the abbreviation for money, as in the economists' money supply measures

explanation.surface: Copper is combined with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cum is a Latin preposition used in English to join two roles, as in kitchen-cum-dining-room, meaning together with.

clue.text: Ferdinand downing very dry Italian favourite

indicators.note: downing, swallowing, says the footballer takes the next letters inside him

parts.note: Rio Ferdinand is the England and Manchester United footballer
so means very, as in so good
TT means teetotal, off drink

explanation.surface: A footballer knocks back a very dry Italian wine he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio Ferdinand is a former England football captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a much-loved Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Each time, special grub

explanation.surface: Every time it is special food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats and grub are both informal words for food.

clue.text: Contain flu outbreak — it's working

indicators.note: outbreak says the letters break out of their order and form a new word

explanation.surface: A public health instruction to control a flu epidemic, which apparently is working.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in working order is operational, running properly as intended.

clue.text: Comedy writer's block?

parts.note: writer's block suggests a comic who cannot write, but block here is a pad of drawing paper; a comedy routine is a sketch

explanation.surface: A joke about a comedian who has run out of ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer's block is the inability to write; here block is a pad of paper, and sketch is a comedy turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of blank pages for drawing on is literally a block, and its contents are sketches.

clue.text: Thump Kelvin's ugly conk

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: ugly says the letters of conk are spoilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone punches a man called Kelvin on his ugly nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Conk is British slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock is to strike or hit hard, a synonym for thump.

clue.text: Family bonds at home in Cambodia's fashionable society

indicators.note: in says the home word goes inside the Cambodian letters

parts.note: K is the international vehicle code for Cambodia, and with its possessive it gives KS
in means at home
hip means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Family ties among the fashionable set back home in Cambodia.
explanation.walkthrough: K is Cambodia's international car registration letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is a blood relationship, so kinships are ties within a family.

clue.text: Difficult to get deposit for a place in Liverpool

parts.note: a knotty problem is a difficult one
ash is the deposit left by a fire or volcano

explanation.surface: It is hard to find a deposit for a house in Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Knotty Ash is a Liverpool district made famous by Ken Dodd, the comedian at 1 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty Ash is a suburb of Liverpool in north-west England.

clue.text: Modern, seething city is revolting

indicators.note: is revolting says the word turns over, read the other way up

parts.note: the Great Wen was William Cobbett's name for the crowded, teeming city of London

explanation.surface: The modern, seething city is in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: A wen is a swelling; Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen', so a wen is a teeming city.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern things are recent, the sense of the word for not old.

clue.text: Late replacement for evening dress?

indicators.note: replacement for says one word swaps in for the first part of the formal garment

parts.note: a formal long gown for women worn after dark
late at night, in the dark hours

explanation.surface: Someone changes out of their evening dress late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the word evening in evening gown for the later NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is what you change into at bedtime, replacing the evening's formal dress.

clue.text: Fish filling our Amish nets

indicators.note: nets, as in catches, says the answer is caught inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fish is caught in the nets of Amish fishermen, stuffing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' looks like part of the definition, but it is where the hidden word starts, with its last G.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourami is a tropical freshwater species of Asia, popular in home aquariums.

clue.text: Folding old uniform for a mate in Paris

parts.note: rig is an outfit or uniform
ami is French for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Folding up an old uniform for a friend in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding, so the noun folding names it.

clue.text: Mum abandoned old Welsh pit town; no good banking savings

indicators.note: banking says the next letters form banks on either side
abandoned says the mother word is left out of the town's name

parts.note: Maesteg is a former coal-mining town in South Wales
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: A mother left an old Welsh mining town that was no good at banking savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Maesteg is in the South Wales valleys, where coal mining was the main industry; 'banking' is the container signal, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, a sum of savings.

clue.text: A wanderer, Matt's heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means read right to left

parts.note: Matt Damon is the American actor

explanation.surface: The actor Matt is a wanderer, heading off west.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams without a settled home, so is one who wanders.

clue.text: Running up shirt seams to dress top musicians

indicators.note: Running up says the hidden letters are read backwards
to dress, to clothe, says the answer is wrapped inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sewing shirts so the top musicians are dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'to dress', but those words are the hidden-word signal and cannot stand for the answer, so the definition is just 'top musicians'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, a great conductor or virtuoso.

clue.text: Most high and mighty at this huge gathering

indicators.note: gathering says the letters are collected together into a new order

explanation.surface: The most arrogant people are at this huge party.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty means arrogantly proud, and its superlative means the proudest, most lordly.

clue.text: Queen escorted by her neighbours from deck in tug

indicators.note: escorted by says the queen is flanked on both sides

parts.note: the queen in a deck of cards sits between the jack and king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: The Queen walks the deck of a tugboat with an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen in a pack sits between jack (J) and king (K).
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sudden sharp pull, the same as a tug.

clue.text: Film company has overdraft; in the smelly stuff by the sound of it

indicators.note: in says the bank letters go inside the spoken slang
by the sound of it says the slang word is to be spelt as it is pronounced

parts.note: cack is British slang for excrement
OD is the bank statement abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: A film company runs up an overdraft and lands in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the cack' is British slang for being in trouble, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Kodak is the photographic company famous for camera film.

clue.text: Missus taking in a bar?

definitions.note: the question mark signals an example: a well-known chocolate bar

indicators.note: taking in says the title holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman, a missus

explanation.surface: A wife is visiting a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, but it is the chocolate kind, the Mars bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the brand of a famous British chocolate bar of nougat and caramel.

clue.text: Lad from Liverpool, at first softly, a churner-out of music

indicators.note: at first says the soft musical term comes ahead of the lad

parts.note: piano is the musical direction to play softly
la is Scouse slang, Liverpool speech for a lad

explanation.surface: A Liverpool lad gently plays a barrel organ.
explanation.walkthrough: Scousers address a young man as 'la'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a self-playing piano that churns out tunes from perforated paper rolls.

clue.text: Time for Gunners to follow up Emirates' opener

indicators.note: to follow up says the gunners come after the first letter
opener says only the first letter of the stadium's name is used

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Time for Arsenal, the Gunners, to follow up their opening game at the Emirates Stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunners suggests Arsenal, who play at the Emirates, but it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, a span of time.

clue.text: Regularly attends influential talks

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of attends is taken

explanation.surface: Someone regularly attends influential lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: TED talks are the widely watched conference lectures on ideas worth spreading.

clue.text: That's funny (in intergalactic Klingon)

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the two words of the bracket

explanation.surface: A joke said in the alien Klingon language from Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tickling amuses you, so a tickling remark is one that is funny.

clue.text: Beginning to sniff instant glue

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of sniff is taken

parts.note: a tick is an instant, as in 'in a tick'

explanation.surface: Someone starts to sniff instant glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to fasten with adhesive, the same as to glue.
